# 六菩薩亦當誦持經

**ID:** T0491
**Volume:** T14
**Category:** 經集部類

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Liù púsà yì dāng sòngchí jīng* (T491) is a one-fascicle Mahāyāna text whose translator is unknown (*shīyì* 失譯, "translator lost"). It enumerates six bodhisattvas whose names should be invoked in daily chanting practice. The text is shorter and earlier in date than the canonical *aṣṭamahābodhisattva* schemes (*Fóshuō bā dà púsà jīng* [KR6i0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0119) = T490), suggesting a stage in the development of Mahāyāna pantheon-systematization before the standardization of the eight bodhisattvas.

**Abstract**

The text witnesses an early phase of the Mahāyāna devotional pantheon — six bodhisattvas rather than the later canonical eight. The six are typically Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, Maitreya, Samantabhadra, and two others (variously). The catalog meta dates the text to "失譯" (translator lost) without dynasty assignment; the standard catalogers locate it in the broad pre-Sui canonical corpus, giving the bracket of 200–600 CE. [僧祐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E7%A5%90) Sēngyòu's *Chū sānzàng jì jí* (Liáng) lists the text without attribution; later catalogs assign it variously.
